title: How hijab dispute is opening new front in Iran-Azerbaijan tensions
gist: Iran's Ali Akbar Velayati used Azerbaijan's school hijab controversy to challenge Baku over its ties with Israel and its fitness to host the 2027 OIC summit. This elevates a domestic dispute into a geopolitical contest over Azerbaijan's standing in the Muslim world.

insights.claim: Ali Akbar Velayati, adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, used Azerbaijan's school hijab controversy to challenge Baku's relationship with Israel in an Oct. 14 post on X.
insights.so_what: Signals senior Iranian officials are now publicly pressuring Baku.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran

insights.claim: Velayati questioned whether Azerbaijan is fit to host the 2027 OIC summit, linking its headscarf restrictions in schools to its warm welcome of Israeli President Herzog at the CICA summit in Baku.
insights.so_what: Could challenge Baku's diplomatic standing and Israel-Azerbaijan ties.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran

insights.claim: Velayati contrasted Turkey leaving the hall during Herzog's speech with Baku's warm welcome.
insights.so_what: Turkey is being used as a rhetorical foil; Ankara may exploit the dispute.
insights.quote: "Turkey left the hall during [Israeli President Isaac] Herzog's speech at the CICA summit, so what did Baku do? A warm welcome."
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran

insights.claim: The intervention marks a shift from Iranian officials' earlier reluctance to comment, as the hijab dispute had been driven largely by hard-line media.
insights.so_what: Escalation from media to official level raises odds of further bilateral deterioration.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
